notes: Round 1 revision, 21 Oct 2026, after the expert critique (gate: fail). ACCESS LIMITS: every City of Vancouver host (vancouver.ca, guidelines/bylaws/council/syc/rezoning.vancouver.ca) still returns HTTP 403 to automated fetch and was not bypassed, so City policy text stays unopened (opened=false) and is never marked verified. The shared WebSearch budget was exhausted, so this round used direct fetches of known primary pages only. NEWLY OPENED: City open-data portal (24 view-cone polygons, 29 Downtown ODP sub-area polygons, stations, 2013 LiDAR DEM metadata), Canadian Aviation Regulations ss.601.23-601.24, Standard 621 (first 200,000 of 233,211 characters, read through a summarising fetch), BC transit-oriented-area page, Vancouver Official Development Plan page, Vancouver Charter ss.565-565.17, 574.61-574.64 and Part XXIV-B, Transport Canada 2026 consultation, 2024 Gazette text, NAV CANADA page, Storeys and Daily Hive pages. The critic's recollections (CBD jobs policy, large-sites thresholds, Green Buildings, public art, bird-friendly guidelines, Hotel as a Service Use, 2023 provincial parking rules in Vancouver's by-law) could not be checked and are recorded unverified. STRUCTURE: still 8 modules. M03 (ODP sheet) merged into M02 (static register); the departure log moved from M02 into M08 (downstream); new M09 (site georeference, datum, height measures). Dependency graph is acyclic: M02, M07, M09 have no upstream; M06, M05 <- M09; M01 <- M07, M09; M04 <- M02, M09; M08 <- M01, M02, M04, M05, M06, M07 (add a CI cycle check over depends_on). KEY FINDINGS: (1) every VTC tower is an obstacle to air navigation under CAR 601.23(1)(d) (above 150 m AGL), so Standard 621 marking and lighting applies, daytime marking is always required above 150 m AGL, and Transport Canada must be notified at least 90 days before construction. (2) The City's open view-cone polygons are 2D with no elevation fields; sampled central-CBD points fall inside QEP cones 3.2.1-3.2.3 (team-derived, approximate), so the cone floor is the likely binding cap on a real CBD block, and floors must come from the Public Views Guidelines or a City assessment. (3) The 600 ft (183 m) Higher Buildings figure is quoted by the City only for the sites across from Bay Parkade; policy heights are site-specific. (4) A city-wide Vancouver ODP replaced the Vancouver Plan on 31 Mar 2026; its effect on downtown policy is unread. (5) Bay Parkade is a hotel plus residential precedent, not an employment-led one. TIME-CRITICAL: registration closes 29 Oct 2026; Q&A closes 3 Nov 2026. Ask Buildner: (a) which uses count toward 9.0, and is FSR gross or zoning floor area; (b) must every tower be 244-305 m, by which height measure and datum; (c) does the brief package give a real location, view cones or the station portal point; (d) may volumes encroach over streets; (e) may the transit link cross under a public street. TEAM ACTIONS: register and download the brief package; download by hand the Higher Buildings Policy (Shape Your City document link https://www.shapeyourcity.ca/51604/widgets/218772/documents/166245), Public Views Guidelines, Downtown ODP, DD schedule and Vancouver ODP and update the unverified rows; email aviation.pac@tc.gc.ca for the detailed 2026 airport-zoning map; email views@vancouver.ca for a View Cone Assessment once a real block is assumed. Shadow, energy and wind are pointers only (CLIM/ENER packets). The brief says its documents are academic, not legal.

modules.name: VTC hard-rules checker
modules.design_question: Does the massing satisfy the VTC hard rules (height band, 9.0 non-residential FSR, site limits, below-grade transit link, submission format), and which results depend on interpretation?
inputs: Layer0.Massing: tower and podium meshes with level planes
P01-M07 fsr_ledger: one named ledger (default gross) and the three use-tier FSRs
P01-M09 site_frame and height table (CTBUH measures per tower)
Layer0.SitePolygon: 79.2 m x 144.8 m block
Layer0.TransitConnection: tagged below-grade path plus the station portal point placed by the user from the brief's site plan
Submission facts (editable): four A2 landscape boards, 10 MB each, English, anonymous, 30 Nov 2026 23:59 London

parameters.name: Tower height H (architectural top, highest occupied floor, tip)
parameters.relationship: Height up -> storey count up at fixed floor-to-floor. Pass only inside 244-305 m (800-1000 ft), measured as set in P01-M09. Greater height raises view-cone and aviation exposure (P01-M04, P01-M05).

parameters.name: Which towers must lie in the band (all vs at least one)
parameters.relationship: Brief wording is 'one or more towers'. Default requires every tower in band; 'at least one' lets a shorter second tower pass. The switch moves pass/fail without moving the design; ask Buildner.

parameters.name: Counted non-residential floor area (tier chosen)
parameters.relationship: Counted area up -> non-residential FSR up in proportion. Site 79.2 x 144.8 m = about 11,468 m2, so 9.0 FSR needs about 103,200 m2 (derived arithmetic, not a brief figure).

parameters.name: Ledger basis (gross vs zoning)
parameters.relationship: Gross counts every enclosed slab; the zoning ledger subtracts exclusions, so FSR falls. The brief's basis is unstated: M01 reads one named ledger (default gross) and flags when the two straddle 9.0.

parameters.name: Containment of above-grade volume (encroachment switch)
parameters.relationship: Coverage up -> fewer storeys for the same area but less open ground for public realm. Volume stays inside the block unless the switch allows air-space encroachment over streets, logged as a departure.

parameters.name: Below-grade transit connection: continuity and off-site length
parameters.relationship: A continuous path from a core to the station portal point, crossing under street outside the polygon, meets 'connecting directly'. Off-site length up -> walking time and City/transit agreements up (MOBI packet).

parameters.name: Level bands holding public-tagged area
parameters.relationship: More bands with public-tagged area -> closer to 'public-facing uses extend vertically'. The brief says 'should', so this is a soft rule.

parameters.name: Interpretation switches (height measure; all towers vs one; use tier; ledger)
parameters.relationship: Each switch moves pass/fail without moving the design, so each is logged as an assumption until Buildner answers (Q&A closes 3 Nov 2026).

parameters.name: Submission format rules (boards, size, file limit, language, anonymity, deadline)
parameters.relationship: Breaking any rule is a submission risk, not a design result. Only the 30 Nov 2026 23:59 London deadline is confirmed on the competition page; the rest comes from the brief extract. Pointer to PRES board layout.

metrics.good: 244-305 m for every tower, CTBUH architectural top from P01-M09 (strict default)
metrics.bad: below 244 m or above 305 m for any tower

metrics.basis: Band 800-1000 ft from the project's extract of the brief PDF (gated, not opened); CTBUH definitions opened. Corrected r1: was labelled verified; treated as unverified until a page and clause is cited.

metrics.name: Non-residential FSR vs 9.0 minimum (default tier 2)
metrics.good: >= 9.0 on the named ledger
metrics.method: Tier-2 area (office + retail + service incl. hotel) / site area, from P01-M07.
metrics.basis: Brief minimum 9.0 non-residential, high-employment floor area (extract, S02 unopened). Corrected r1: was labelled verified.

metrics.name: Interpretation state of the 9.0 test
metrics.good: tier 1 (office only) >= 9.0: passes under every reading (green)
metrics.bad: tier 3 (all non-residential) < 9.0: fails under every reading (red); between is amber 'needs interpretation'
metrics.method: Compare tiers 1-3 and the zoning-ledger value against 9.0; amber also when gross >= 9.0 > zoning.
metrics.basis: Wording gap in the brief ('office, commercial'); question for Buildner.

metrics.name: Site boundary containment
metrics.good: all above-grade volume inside the polygon of about 11,470 m2 (tolerance editable, default 0.1 m)
metrics.bad: any above-grade volume outside the polygon without the encroachment switch
metrics.method: Extruded-polygon containment test.
metrics.basis: Brief gives only an approximate size, no containment or no-cantilever rule: team assumption.

metrics.good: tagged below-grade path continuous from a core to the user-placed station portal point
metrics.bad: absent or discontinuous; off-site length reported as a flag
metrics.method: Graph path from a core node to the portal point, allowing off-site below-grade segments.
metrics.basis: Requirement from the brief extract (unopened); the path test is a team method because the brief puts the station diagonally across the intersection.

metrics.good: >= 3 bands (base, mid, upper) contain public-tagged area
metrics.method: Count distinct level bands with public, cultural/civic or amenity tags.
metrics.basis: Team preset (editable); brief only says 'should extend vertically'.

metrics.good: all six rules met (4 boards, A2 landscape, <= 10 MB each, English, no identifying information, before 30 Nov 2026 23:59 London)
metrics.method: Checklist ticked by the user; file sizes read from exports.
metrics.basis: Deadline confirmed on the competition page (opened); other rules from the brief extract.

modules.method: 1) Read the site polygon and compute its area (Shapely): 79.2 x 144.8 m = about 11,468 m2. 2) Take H_arch, H_occ and H_tip per tower from P01-M09 (CTBUH measures). 3) Read one named ledger from P01-M07 (default gross; zoning ledger shown beside it); FSR = tier area / site area for tiers 1-3. 4) Test that all above-grade mesh lies inside the polygon within tolerance; the encroachment switch logs a departure. 5) Build a graph of tagged below-grade spaces; test a path from a core node to the user-placed station portal point, allowing off-site segments; report off-site length. 6) Count level bands with public tags. 7) Tick the submission checklist. 8) Emit one record per check: value, threshold, state (pass / fail / needs interpretation / unknown), switches used, source id. No rule silently passes; missing tags give 'unknown'.

Elevation silhouette of each tower on a metre ruler with the 244-305 m band shaded and 800/1000 ft ticks; three heights marked per tower

fsr_nonres_tier1, fsr_nonres_tier2, fsr_nonres_tier3: dimensionless, on the named ledger
modules.human_judgment: Reading ambiguous brief wording (uses counted as non-residential, height measure, all towers or one); deciding to breach a rule on purpose and arguing it; asking Buildner before 3 Nov 2026. Jury link: urban_integration_10 (transit entrance) and human_scale_40 (public uses up the tower); height and FSR are eligibility checks, not design merit.

The package may also contain a site plan, 3D model, station portal and view cones: check it first. The checker tests geometry and tags, not design quality. The brief is academic and the jury may reward justified breaches, so failures are flags.

modules.name: Policy, zoning and CBD land-use register
modules.effort: S-M: about 5 person-days, plus monthly register updates
modules.design_question: Which Vancouver, provincial and federal documents govern a tall tower here, what is each one's status and clause, and which rows are still unverified?
inputs: Static policy register (JSON): document, version, date, status, URL, clause, opened flag
User-entered Downtown ODP and DD schedule values (FSR min and max, parking, loading), typed from the PDFs
Higher Buildings policy-area flag and site height set by the user from the policy's Figure 1
Pointer rows handed to CLIM, ENER, MOBI and P01-M04/M05

parameters.name: Policy status and version date
parameters.relationship: Newer or under-review documents change which clause applies. Higher Buildings draft policies are due fall 2026-winter 2027 and the hearing spring 2027, so every result stays provisional until then.

parameters.name: Higher Buildings policy-area membership and site-specific height
parameters.relationship: Inside the area, allowed height differs by site (summaries cite about 700 ft on Georgia/Burrard/Granville, 425-500 ft at bridgeheads; unverified). The City quotes 600 ft (183 m) only for sites across from Bay Parkade. Outside: rezoning on its merits.

parameters.name: Downtown ODP sub-area
parameters.relationship: The sub-area (letters A-O, K1-K3, L1-L2, C2 in the City's 29 polygons) selects permitted uses and FSR minimum and maximum. Which letter is the CBD core is read from the ODP. A hypothetical block makes this an assumption that moves every cap.

parameters.name: FSR minimum and maximum, interpretive height, relaxation
parameters.relationship: Cap up -> permitted floor area up; above it, density needs bonus or CD-1 rezoning. ODP height provisions are interpretive and relaxable by the Development Permit Board, so zoning alone does not cap a supertall. Values are typed from the PDF.

parameters.name: CBD land-use designation and job-space policy
parameters.relationship: If residential is restricted in the CBD core and job space protected (Metro Core Jobs and Economy plan, reviewer recollection, unverified), the residential share becomes a departure and replacement rules may apply; VTC's 9.0 minimum may mirror it.

parameters.name: Parking cap, loading minimum and transit-oriented area
parameters.relationship: Inside a transit-oriented area (within 800 m of a rapid transit station) local governments cannot require off-street residential parking; accessible, commercial parking and loading may still be required. Parking cap down -> fewer below-grade levels.

parameters.name: Rezoning policies likely triggered
parameters.relationship: Large-site sustainability policy (thresholds 0.8 ha or 45,000 m2 recalled, unverified), Green Buildings Policy for Rezonings, public art and bird-friendly guidelines each add submissions and design duties. The block (about 1.15 ha, over 103,000 m2 non-residential) would exceed both thresholds if recalled correctly.

parameters.name: Zoning path (outright, relaxation, CD-1)
parameters.relationship: A CD-1 sets site-specific height, FSR and conditions; Bay Parkade's sets only a maximum height. Council's May 2023 direction sends non-conforming schemes to rezoning on their merits. The path sets the scale of the benefits negotiation (P01-M08).

parameters.name: Precedent register (Bay Parkade rezoning, 27 Jul 2026, 7-3)
parameters.relationship: Council accepted three towers above policy heights with a large benefits package. The scheme is hotel plus residential, outside the policy area: evidence of a path for height beyond policy, not a rule and not a program precedent.

parameters.name: Pointer rows: shadow, wind, energy, public views, aviation
parameters.relationship: Rows name the governing documents handed on: shadow criteria for named parks and plazas and wind comfort (CLIM), energy and emissions limits (ENER), cones (P01-M04), airspace (P01-M05). All unverified until read.

metrics.name: Policy-area height reference (lookup)
metrics.good: site-specific value read from the policy's Figure 1 and typed with its clause
metrics.bad: one universal 600 ft figure applied to any site
metrics.method: Lookup by policy-area site. 600 ft (183 m) is stored only for 'sites immediately across the street' from Bay Parkade; other sites stay unknown (grey hatched); the summarised 700 ft and 425-500 ft figures are stored as unverified.
metrics.basis: City FAQ (opened) ties 600 ft to the sites across from Bay Parkade; 2011 and 2018 summaries give site-specific heights; policy PDFs unopened. Corrected r1: was a universal verified threshold.

metrics.name: Review-status banner
metrics.good: every policy-based result carries 'provisional: review in progress, hearing spring 2027'
metrics.method: Banner on every node that reads a register row.
metrics.basis: City project page: draft policies fall 2026-winter 2027; hearing and adoption spring 2027.

metrics.name: Register completeness
metrics.good: every row has status, URL, opened flag and clause or 'not read'
metrics.method: Count complete rows / total.
metrics.basis: Course rule that every result cites its source (team preset).

metrics.name: Register freshness
metrics.good: <= 14 days before 30 Nov 2026 (editable)
metrics.method: Date stamp per register row.
metrics.basis: Team preset: review drafts and Bay Parkade follow-ups are moving targets.

modules.name: Public view-cone checker
modules.effort: L: about 8-12 person-days (manual-parameter and hypothetical-cone modes, about 4 days, are core; open-data ingestion 4-8 days is v1)
modules.design_question: Does the massing penetrate a protected public view cone (Queen Elizabeth Park or others), by how much, and does that trigger a Higher Buildings special review?
inputs: Layer0.Massing; highest physical point per tower from P01-M09 in the cone's datum
P01-M09 site_frame: assumed real block, ground elevation, vertical datum
Cone polygons: City open data (24 cones, 2D, dated), or cones supplied in the brief package if any
Cone floors and azimuths typed from the Public Views Guidelines or a City View Cone Assessment (views@vancouver.ca)
P01-M02 hb_policy_area flag
Context massing (existing and approved towers), optional

parameters.name: Cone lower-boundary elevation at the site
parameters.relationship: Cone floor up -> allowable top up; allowable height = cone floor - ground elevation. Older documents suggest floors near 100-145 m at downtown sites, far below 244-305 m (derived, unverified). The open dataset carries no elevations.

parameters.name: Footprint position relative to the cone polygon
parameters.relationship: Footprint outside the polygon -> no penetration at any height; inside, every metre above the cone floor penetrates. Team check: sampled CBD points fell inside QEP cones 3.2.1-3.2.3 (2D, approximate coordinates; re-run on the real block).

parameters.name: View origin and subject
parameters.relationship: The origin is the camera for the skyline view; moving it changes every result. The four QEP polygons share a southern apex near 49.242 N (derived from polygon extents). The brief requires one skyline view from the QEP viewpoint.

parameters.name: Cone status after 10 Jul 2024 (retained, updated, eliminated)
parameters.relationship: QEP 3.2.1-3.2.4 were retained and not updated; 3.1 and 3.2.4a were eliminated; 11 other cones were updated. Retained cones' pre-2024 geometry may still hold (confirm); eliminated cones are not tested.

parameters.name: Higher Buildings site status
parameters.relationship: Only select downtown Higher Buildings sites may enter QEP cone boundaries, through a special review (City page summary, unopened). Elsewhere penetration is not an option. The 2026 review does not revise protected views.

parameters.name: Ground elevation at the tower
parameters.relationship: Ground elevation up -> allowable height above grade down for a fixed cone floor (arithmetic). Taken from P01-M09 (City 2013 LiDAR DEM or typed).

parameters.name: Highest physical point tested (spire, plant, rig)
parameters.relationship: Rooftop plant, antennae and window-washing rigs count in a cone test, so penetration uses the highest physical point, not the CTBUH architectural top, in the cone's vertical datum.

parameters.name: Angular width of the tower from the origin
parameters.relationship: Width up -> more of the mountain skyline covered. No sourced acceptable-occlusion threshold found (see unresolved relationships).

metrics.name: Maximum penetration per cone
metrics.good: 0 m (all parts outside the cone)
metrics.method: Max over vertices and subdivided edges of (z_highest_point - cone_floor); 'unknown' when no floor is entered.
metrics.basis: Search summary of the Public Views Guidelines: all parts of a building should lie outside cone boundaries. PDF unopened.

metrics.name: Higher Buildings review trigger
metrics.good: no penetration, or penetration only at an identified Higher Buildings site with review planned
metrics.bad: penetration at a site not in the policy area
metrics.method: Penetration > 0 AND hb_policy_area flag from P01-M02.
metrics.basis: City page summary of the special review; policy area map unopened.

metrics.name: Cone dataset vintage and per-cone status
metrics.good: dataset dated after 10 Jul 2024 (City open data modified 19 Oct 2026, 24 cones) and each cone tagged retained or updated
metrics.bad: 38-cone pre-2024 data for an updated cone, or any test of an eliminated cone
metrics.method: Check dataset date and cone id against the Storeys list; retained cones may use older geometry with an 'unverified, confirm unchanged' badge.
metrics.basis: Council replaced the View Protection Guidelines on 10 Jul 2024. Corrected r1: the claim that pre-2024 data overstates restriction is false for retained QEP cones 3.2.1-3.2.4.

metrics.name: Cone-floor data present
metrics.good: floors and azimuths typed from a City document or the brief, with source id
metrics.bad: no floor values: result 'unknown' (grey hatched), never pass
metrics.method: Required field per cone; hypothetical-cone mode shows the floor in team-assumption colour and gives no pass/fail.
metrics.basis: Open dataset has polygons only; hypothetical block.

metrics.name: Occlusion of the mountain skyline from the origin
metrics.good: 0% (team target)
metrics.bad: any occlusion; severity judged by people
metrics.method: Ray grid from the origin through the cone window; share of rays hitting the massing before the subject.
metrics.basis: Team preset; no sourced threshold.

modules.method: 1) Check the brief package for cones, a real location or a station portal; use them as the default (S02). 2) If absent, pick an assumed real block in P01-M09 (team assumption) or use 'hypothetical cone' mode with an editable floor and no pass/fail. 3) Load the 24 City cone polygons (2D) with their date; tag each retained, updated or eliminated. 4) Type cone floors and azimuths from the Public Views Guidelines or a City View Cone Assessment. 5) For each vertex and subdivided edge of the highest-point set inside a wedge compute margin = z - cone_floor; penetration = max margin. 6) Cast rays from the origin across the cone window (three-mesh-bvh) against massing and context towers. 7) Render the origin-point view for the PRES skyline image. Missing floors give 'unknown'.
visualization: Plan: cone polygons in translucent colour by status (retained, updated), origin point, site outline
Section along the cone axis: cone floor line, tower, penetrating part in red
Origin-point panorama: cone window outline, mountain subject, tower silhouette against context towers (also feeds the PRES skyline view; shown without pass/fail in hypothetical mode)
False-colour on the tower mesh: green below the cone to red above, legend 0-200 m penetration
outputs: view_cone_report: list per cone {cone_id, status_2024, penetration_m, margin_m, state, source_id}
cone_data_gaps: list of cones without floors
modules.human_judgment: Whether penetration is justified; judging skyline silhouette and the 'City in Nature' relationship; requesting an official View Cone Assessment for a real parcel; moving towers to avoid cones. Jury link: cultural_context_30 (views to the North Shore mountains) and design_excellence_20 (skyline contribution).
modules.limits: The Public Views Guidelines PDF and VanMap returned HTTP 403. The open dataset has polygons but no elevations, so cone floors are user-supplied; figures such as 322.8 ft (1997) and 361 ft (2022) are historical or site-specific. The block is hypothetical: cone results exist only after an assumed real location and datum.

modules.name: Airspace height screening and obstruction marking
modules.effort: S-M: about 4-5 person-days (marking and checklist 2; optional surface heightfields 2-3)
modules.design_question: Could federal aviation rules (YVR zoning, NAV CANADA procedures, harbour aerodromes) cap tower height, which obstruction marking and lighting apply, and what must the team file or ask?
inputs: Highest physical point per tower, AGL and AMSL, from P01-M09 (roof additions count)
Site latitude/longitude from P01-M09
Optional heliport FATO position, approach azimuth, number of paths, performance class
Optional Transport Canada map or surface heights; crane height assumption

parameters.name: Highest physical point, AGL and AMSL
parameters.relationship: Top up -> more likely to penetrate an obstacle surface or instrument procedure and to need NAV CANADA mitigation. A roof mast counts toward height (CAR 601.23(2)). At Bay Parkade, City staff relayed that about 27 m (88 ft) may need cutting.

parameters.name: Obstacle status under CAR 601.23
parameters.relationship: A structure above 150 m AGL is an obstacle; above 90 m AGL it is one within 6 km of an aerodrome's geographical centre or 3.7 km of a VFR route. Every VTC tower qualifies, so Standard 621 marking and lighting apply.

parameters.name: Marking and lighting configuration
parameters.relationship: Above 150 m AGL daytime marking is always required, even with medium-intensity white lights; high-intensity white (CL-856) is an option; strobe-type lights are not recommended in urban areas; glare shielding may be needed. The choice shapes crown and facade design.

parameters.name: Distance and bearing to YVR runway strips
parameters.relationship: Under SOR/80-902 approach surfaces rise 1 m per 50 m to 15 km along runway centrelines; outer limits are described mainly in Richmond and along the Richmond-Vancouver boundary. No opened source puts downtown inside: applicability unknown, probably outside.

parameters.name: Proposed 2026 zoning extension
parameters.relationship: The July 2026 consultation adds an area covering much of Vancouver north of the Fraser, west to English Bay, to the April 2024 proposal. If the CBD is inside, a new surface may cap new towers. Heights are unpublished; request the map.

parameters.name: Existing taller buildings under the 2024 proposal
parameters.relationship: In the 2024 text, buildings existing at entry into force become legally non-conforming and may not be raised. The 2026 page is silent on this. Exceptions ('bump-outs') were granted in five specific areas, Richmond among them.

parameters.name: Heliport surfaces (operator impact)
parameters.relationship: Standard 325 sets heliport certification surfaces: non-instrument approach 245 m at 6-10%, then 830 m at 16%; transitional 50% to 45 m. A building penetrating them affects the heliport's certification; it is not barred. Heliport, FATO and class are unknown.

parameters.name: Instrument procedures and harbour water aerodrome (CYHC)
parameters.relationship: NAV CANADA instrument-procedure obstacle clearance and floatplane and helicopter routes near Coal Harbour may bind height more than any zoning surface. Not modelled; carried as named unknowns for NAV CANADA to answer.

parameters.name: Assessment and notice timing
parameters.relationship: NAV CANADA attempts replies in 8-12 weeks, which 'can go up to 12 to 18 months pending necessary mitigations' in or around an airport; the letter is not a permit. Transport Canada notice is due 90 days before construction. Late filing risks floor cuts.

metrics.name: Marking and lighting plan declared
metrics.good: Standard 621 system chosen for each tower and Transport Canada notice logged at least 90 days before construction
metrics.bad: no plan, or notice after design freeze
metrics.method: Checklist with dates; marking_lighting_required is true for every tower above 150 m AGL.
metrics.basis: CAR 601.23(1)(d), 601.24 and Standard 621 s.2.5 and s.4.2 (opened).

metrics.name: YVR zoning surface penetration (formula)
metrics.good: <= 0 m, or site outside the outer limits

modules.name: Tower siting, separation and floor plate
modules.design_question: Do tower positions, floor plates, street walls and separations from on-site and neighbouring existing or approved towers meet downtown guidelines for each use, and which departures need justification?
inputs: Layer0.Towers: floor-plate polygon per level, with use tags (residential, office, hotel)
Layer0.Podium and site edges (streets, lanes)
Context massing tagged existing or approved-not-built
P01-M09 site_frame: grid-to-true-north rotation

parameters.name: Tower-to-tower separation above podium, by use
parameters.relationship: Separation up -> daylight, privacy and sky view up, usable footprint down. A residential candidate of 24.4 m (80 ft) is recalled from Downtown South practice, unverified; office and hotel bands have no known value. The brief asks entrants to consider spacing.

parameters.name: Cross-street separation
parameters.relationship: Towers across a street or lane: separation up with street width, usable plate down. No sourced value; computed from facade normals and reported, not graded.

parameters.name: Floor-plate area and width by level and use
parameters.relationship: Plate width up -> shadow width and wind-facing width up (quantified in CLIM packets), slenderness down. A residential candidate near 6,500 sq ft (about 604 m2) is recalled, unverified; no downtown office or hotel cap was found.

parameters.name: Street-wall (podium) height and setbacks
parameters.relationship: Podium height up -> stronger street wall and more shelter, less sky view from the street; setback to lot lines and lanes up -> public realm and lane width up, plate area down. No sourced value for Georgia-type streets.

parameters.name: Distance to approved-not-built towers
parameters.relationship: Closer approved towers in the same height range -> separation shrinks and needs negotiation. Context must include approved towers such as Bay Parkade.

parameters.name: Grid-to-true-north rotation
parameters.relationship: Rotation decides which facade faces which compass direction in sun, wind and energy modules. Read from P01-M09; the brief's north arrow is rotated against the street grid.

metrics.name: Minimum tower-to-tower separation, residential bands only
metrics.good: >= 24.4 m (80 ft) (candidate, editable)
metrics.method: Minimum polygon distance and facade-normal distance per residential band above podium; office and hotel bands return 'unknown'.
metrics.basis: Recalled residential guideline value; no City guideline could be opened.

metrics.name: Residential floor-plate area (candidate cap)
metrics.good: <= about 604 m2 (6,500 sq ft), editable
metrics.method: Slab polygon area per residential level.
metrics.basis: Recalled residential practice; not found in an opened source.

metrics.name: Office and hotel floor-plate band
metrics.good: inside the team-entered band (no default supplied)
metrics.bad: outside the band; 'unknown' when no band is entered
metrics.method: Area per level from slab polygons.
metrics.basis: No sourced downtown floor-plate cap for office or hotel; team setting.

metrics.name: Context completeness
metrics.good: all existing and approved towers within the review radius (editable) are in the model
metrics.method: Compare the context list with the City's approved-tower list.
metrics.basis: Brief context includes existing high-rises and approved towers.

modules.method: Slice each tower into level bands above the podium (Shapely) and tag each band by dominant use. For every tower pair, on-site and context, compute the minimum polygon distance and, for facing facades, the perpendicular distance along facade normals; keep the minimum per band. Compute floor-plate area, perimeter and bounding width per level, plus podium height and setbacks to lot lines and lanes. Compute each facade's grid and true bearing using the rotation from P01-M09. Apply thresholds only to the uses they were recalled for: residential candidates grade residential bands; office and hotel bands return 'unknown' unless the team enters a band. Return a pair matrix, cross-street distances and closest pairs. Approved-not-built towers are drawn hatched.
visualization: Plan with separation lines coloured green (meets), red (below), amber (unverified threshold), grey (no threshold) and distances labelled
Elevation strip showing sky corridors between towers by level band
Floor-plate area bar chart by level and use with the team band shaded
Context towers coloured by status: existing, approved, proposed; approved-not-built drawn with hatched outline
outputs: separation_matrix: pair x band distances, m
floor_plate_table: area, width per level and use
modules.human_judgment: Judging tower rhythm, views between towers and urban-design quality; deciding to depart from a guideline; anticipating the final form of approved neighbours. Jury link: human_scale_40 (sky corridors, daylight, street wall) and design_excellence_20.
modules.limits: No City guideline PDF on tower separation, floor plate or street wall could be opened. 24.4 m and 604 m2 are recalled residential candidates and must not be applied to office or hotel towers. Approved-but-unbuilt towers may change. Shadow, wind and daylight consequences belong to the CLIM packets.

modules.name: Program and FSR accounting
modules.effort: M: about 5-7 person-days (ledger 4, use tiers and core allocation 2-3)
modules.design_question: How much floor area counts toward total FSR and the 9.0 non-residential minimum under gross and zoning accounting, and how sensitive is compliance to use tiers, core allocation and exclusions?
inputs: Layer0 program-tagged slab polygons by level (or IFC spaces or mesh volumes)
Site area (gross, optionally net of dedications)
Exclusion preset (editable list with clause ids)
Use-tier switch (tiers 1-3) and core/mechanical allocation switch

parameters.name: Accounting basis (gross vs zoning ledger)
parameters.relationship: Gross counts every enclosed slab; the zoning ledger subtracts listed exclusions, so FSR goes down. The brief's own basis is unstated, so both ledgers are shown and one is named for P01-M01.

parameters.name: Exclusion rules (example set)
parameters.relationship: Each enabled exclusion -> counted area down -> FSR down. CD-1 by-law examples (site-specific): parking, loading, mechanical at or below base surface; balconies to 8%; amenity to 1,000 m2; storage 3.7 m2 per unit; wall allowance 152 mm.

parameters.name: Use tier for the 9.0 minimum
parameters.relationship: Tier 1 office; tier 2 adds retail and service uses incl. hotel; tier 3 adds cultural/civic, public and non-residential amenity. Residential amenity never counts. Each step raises non-residential FSR without changing the design.

parameters.name: Hotel classification
parameters.relationship: Hotel in tier 2 follows ordinary 'commercial' usage; the Zoning and Development By-law is recalled (unverified) to list Hotel under Service Uses. Moving hotel in or out changes FSR by hotel area / site area.

parameters.name: Core, circulation and mechanical allocation
parameters.relationship: Sharing core and mechanical area out to uses by served floor area raises office FSR; leaving them as separate tags understates it. More mechanical floors -> gross area and height up; exclusions decide whether they count.

parameters.name: Site-area basis
parameters.relationship: Site area down (for example after dedications) -> FSR up for the same floor area. The brief gives only a gross block size.

metrics.name: Non-residential FSR, tier 1 (office only)
metrics.good: >= 9.0: passes under every reading
metrics.method: Office area / site area on the named ledger.
metrics.basis: 9.0 minimum from the brief extract (S02 unopened); tier definitions are team presets.

metrics.name: Non-residential FSR, tier 2 (office + retail + service incl. hotel; default claim reading)
metrics.method: Tier-2 area, core and mechanical shared out when the switch is on, / site area.
metrics.basis: Brief wording 'office, commercial' (extract). Corrected r1: was a 'strict' reading labelled verified, with hotel excluded and core unallocated.

metrics.name: Non-residential FSR, tier 3 (all non-residential)
metrics.good: >= 9.0 (weakest reading)
metrics.method: Adds cultural/civic, public and non-residential amenity; residential amenity excluded.
metrics.basis: Brief wording gap; team presets.

metrics.name: Interpretation gap (tier 3 minus tier 1)
metrics.good: gap does not change pass/fail
metrics.bad: tier 1 < 9.0 <= tier 3: result depends on interpretation
metrics.method: Three tiers run side by side.
metrics.basis: Wording gap in the brief; ask Buildner.

metrics.name: Total FSR (all uses)
metrics.good: reported only; no overall cap in the brief extract
metrics.method: All counted area / site area; compare with Bay Parkade 27.4 (press, consolidated site) for orientation only.
metrics.basis: Brief extract (unopened); press figure from Storeys (opened).

metrics.name: Ledger reconciliation and exclusion documentation
metrics.good: level totals equal the ledger total, untagged area 0, 100% of exclusions carry a clause id and status
metrics.bad: any mismatch, untagged area or exclusion without a clause
metrics.method: Count documented / total; sum check.
metrics.basis: Course rule: show work and sources.

modules.method: Per level and tag, sum slab polygon areas (Shapely) or IfcSpace quantities (IfcOpenShell). Build two ledgers: gross (all enclosed floor area) and zoning (gross minus enabled exclusions, each with a clause id and status). When the switch is on, share core, circulation and mechanical area out to uses by served floor area. Divide by site area. Compute non-residential FSR for tier 1 (office), tier 2 (adds retail and service uses including hotel) and tier 3 (adds cultural/civic, public and non-residential amenity); residential amenity is never counted. Run one-at-a-time sensitivity on each exclusion, tier and allocation switch. Reconcile the ledger total with level totals; warn on untagged slab area. CD-1 exclusion values are shown as 'unverified examples', never as Downtown District rules.
visualization: Stacked bar by level (y = floor, x = m2) coloured by program tag
Waterfall: gross GFA -> exclusions -> counted area -> tier 1, 2, 3 non-residential
FSR gauge with the 9.0 line; three tier markers and a ghost marker for the zoning ledger
Tornado chart of FSR change per switch
outputs: fsr_ledger: level x tag table, gross and zoning
fsr_nonres_tier1, fsr_nonres_tier2, fsr_nonres_tier3: numbers, gross and zoning
allocation_report: core and mechanical shares by use
modules.human_judgment: Classifying mixed or ambiguous spaces; choosing which interpretation to claim; defending exclusions and the hotel classification to the jury; confirming wording with Buildner. Jury link: design_excellence_20 (programme diagram, compliance).
modules.limits: Vancouver's exclusion rules in the Zoning and Development By-law and DD schedule were not read (HTTP 403); CD-1 values are site-specific examples; hotel as a Service Use is recalled. Massing-stage areas are approximate; net areas need core and MEP presets from other packets. Not a plan check.

modules.name: Departure log and public-benefit ledger
modules.effort: M: about 6-7 person-days (departure log 3, core; benefit ledger and tool mapping 3-4, v1)
modules.design_question: Where does the scheme depart from policy, what public benefits does it offer for that density and height, and which statutory or policy tool covers each?
inputs: Rule results from P01-M01, P01-M04, P01-M05, P01-M06, P01-M07
policy_register, zoning_envelope and hb_policy_area from P01-M02
gfa_by_tag from P01-M07 (public, cultural/civic, amenity areas)
Public-realm and plaza areas from Layer 0
Non-floor benefit items (transit entrance, free-access deck) with user values
User departure notes: free text plus evidence source ids

parameters.name: Written departure rationale
parameters.relationship: A sourced rationale per departure turns a breach into an argument. The brief states the jury may reward justified breaches. The tool never writes the rationale.

parameters.name: Height beyond policy
parameters.relationship: Height above the site's policy height -> larger departure. Every VTC tower (244-305 m) exceeds 600 ft (183 m) and the summarised 700 ft (213 m), so each needs a record with clause, values, delta, evidence and jury tag.

parameters.name: Density above base
parameters.relationship: The Charter allows base density plus higher density when amenities or affordable units are provided, so more extra FSR requested -> more benefit expected. No formula was found.

parameters.name: Form of benefit (five categories)
parameters.relationship: In-kind conditions (s.565(1)(f.1), s.565.17); payment in lieu (s.565.13); DCL (s.523D); ACC (s.523E, in-kind s.523M); negotiated policy CAC (not statutory). An ACC cannot apply where a DCL may be imposed (s.523I(2)).

parameters.name: Free-access floor area given
parameters.relationship: Free-access area up -> benefit up, saleable area down. Bay Parkade secured free resident access to its observation deck by rezoning condition.

parameters.name: Transit entrance and public plaza as benefits
parameters.relationship: Bay Parkade counted new street-level and underground station entrances and a plaza among its benefits, so VTC's below-grade entrance can be logged as a benefit item.

parameters.name: Plan-area contribution expectations
parameters.relationship: The Granville Street Plan (approved 4 Jun 2025) lists a development contribution expectations policy; if the block lies in or near the plan area its terms apply. Text not read.

parameters.name: Other rezoning obligations as benefit categories
parameters.relationship: Affordable housing, public art and large-site sustainability measures (recalled, unverified) are separate benefit categories beside CACs; each needs its own ledger line and tool tag.

parameters.name: Precedent fit (Bay Parkade)
parameters.relationship: Hotel plus residential, no office, outside the policy area; 27.4 FSR consolidated; storeys differ by source. Fit is height beyond policy, aviation risk and benefit scale, not program or the 9.0 non-residential test.

metrics.name: Departure log completeness
metrics.good: 100% of departures have rationale, evidence id and jury tag
metrics.method: Count complete records / total; every fail, amber or unknown rule result must have a record or an 'accepted' note.
metrics.basis: Course rule that every result cites its source (team preset).

metrics.name: Height delta vs policy reference
metrics.good: <= the site's Figure 1 height once read (600 ft only for sites across from Bay Parkade)
metrics.bad: above it: departure required; 'unknown' when the site height is not entered
metrics.method: Each tower's H_arch minus the reference from P01-M02.
metrics.basis: Policy PDFs unopened; City FAQ for the 600 ft case.

metrics.name: Benefit-to-tool mapping completeness
metrics.good: 100% of benefit items mapped to in-kind condition, payment in lieu, DCL, ACC or policy CAC (policy, unverified)
metrics.method: Count mapped / total.
metrics.basis: Vancouver Charter ss.565, 565.1, 565.13, 565.17, 523D, 523E, 523I, 523M (opened). Corrected r1: cash CAC is policy-based, not a Charter charge.

metrics.name: Public-benefit floor-area share
metrics.good: team sets a target (no sourced value)
metrics.method: Free-access public, civic and amenity GFA / total GFA.
metrics.basis: Team preset; no sourced threshold.

metrics.name: Bay Parkade benchmark panel
metrics.good: shown with a precedent-fit note (program, policy-area status, height measure) and labelled press and staff figures
metrics.bad: shown as a benchmark for an employment-led tower
metrics.method: Report only: cash CAC about $20 million, in-kind about $184 million, package about $305 million, 27.4 FSR.
metrics.basis: Daily Hive and Storeys (opened); hotel plus residential, outside the policy area. Corrected r1: not a program benchmark.

metrics.name: Jury linkage
metrics.good: every benefit and departure tagged to a jury criterion
metrics.method: Count tagged / total.
metrics.basis: Team preset.

modules.method: 1) Collect rule results from P01-M01, M04, M05, M06, M07 and register rows from M02. 2) For every fail, amber or unknown result and every policy the design departs from, require a departure record: clause, design value, policy value, delta, rationale, evidence ids, jury tag. 3) Draw the height ladder (183 m, 213 m, VTC band, towers, Bay Parkade 238.59, 270.97, 314.89 m, and the 288 m marker labelled 'measure unstated'). 4) Build the benefit ledger (item, type, area or value, free-access flag, tool, jury tag, source) and map each item to in-kind condition, payment in lieu, DCL, ACC or policy CAC. 5) Compute the public floor-area share from M07 tags. 6) Show the Bay Parkade panel with the precedent-fit note. 7) Export markdown for the policy reflection. The tool never writes rationale or estimates the City's CAC, which is negotiated from a land-lift analysis.
visualization: Height ladder in metres: 183 m (600 ft), 213 m (700 ft), VTC band 244-305 m, each tower as a marker, Bay Parkade towers and the 288 m marker hatched
Clause table with pass, depart, n.a. badges linked to source ids; FALSE ASSUMPTION rows in fixed magenta
Sankey (d3-sankey) from density above base to benefit items to tools
Benchmark bars: scheme vs Bay Parkade for cash, in-kind and floor-area share, labelled press and staff figures
Matrix of benefit items and departures against the four jury criteria
outputs: departure_register: list of {clause, design_value, policy_value, delta, rationale, evidence_ids, jury_tag}
policy_reflection_text: markdown for the PRES boards
modules.human_judgment: Whether and why to depart; what counts as a real public benefit; Indigenous and community partnership content (CULT packet); economic viability; negotiating the package; all policy-reflection writing. Jury link: human_scale_40 and cultural_context_30 (benefits), design_excellence_20 (departures).
modules.limits: Vancouver's CAC and density-bonus policies, current DCL rates and any Vancouver ACC by-law were not opened, so no rates or percentages are given. Whether the large-site policy applies to a block of about 1.15 ha is unconfirmed. Precedent figures are press and staff figures as reported. Not a pro forma.

modules.name: Site georeference, datum and height measures
modules.effort: S: about 3 person-days (transforms and height converter), plus 1 day to load City DEM and cone data
modules.design_question: Where is the hypothetical block, what are its ground elevation, vertical datum and grid rotation, and how do tower heights convert between brief, CTBUH, view-cone and aviation measures?
inputs: Layer0.Massing with level planes
Assumed block (lat/long or City parcel pick), or the brief's site plan and 3D model if they give a location
North-arrow rotation read from the brief's site plan (deg)
Optional City 2013 LiDAR DEM tile or a typed ground elevation
Station portal point from the brief's site plan

parameters.name: Assumed real location of the block
parameters.relationship: Moving the block along the peninsula changes the ODP sub-area, view cones, airspace surfaces and ground elevation that apply. Results in P01-M02, M04 and M05 are valid only for the recorded assumption (team assumption until the brief gives a site).

parameters.name: Ground elevation at the tower base
parameters.relationship: Ground elevation up -> top elevation above sea level up by the same amount for a fixed height above grade, so allowable height above grade under a cone or surface falls by that amount (arithmetic). City DEM cells are about 1 m.

parameters.name: Vertical datum of each dataset (CGVD28 vs CGVD2013)
parameters.relationship: A datum mismatch shifts every cone and aviation test by the offset between datums (assumed sub-metre, unverified). Record the datum of cone documents, DEM and aviation data before comparing; the City DEM description states none.

parameters.name: Grid-to-true-north rotation
parameters.relationship: Rotation up -> every facade bearing shifts by the same angle in sun, wind and energy modules. The brief's north arrow is rotated against the street grid; the value is read from the site plan.

parameters.name: Height measure (architectural top, highest occupied floor, tip, highest physical point)
parameters.relationship: Each measure adds or removes rooftop elements: CTBUH architectural top excludes antennae, while aviation height counts roof additions such as a mast (CAR 601.23(2)). Cone and aviation tests therefore use the highest physical point.

parameters.name: Reference level for CTBUH height
parameters.relationship: CTBUH measures from the lowest significant open-air pedestrian entrance. On a sloping downtown block a lower reference entrance -> reported height up by the difference, which can flip the 244-305 m test.

parameters.name: Ground point that defines AGL for aviation
parameters.relationship: Which ground point (lowest, highest or footprint centroid) defines AGL on a sloping block is not stated in the text read; a different choice moves the 150 m and 90 m tests by the slope across the footprint.

metrics.name: Height conversion traceability
metrics.good: 100% of heights passed to P01-M01, M04, M05 carry measure, datum and ground reference
metrics.method: Type check on every height output.
metrics.basis: Course rule: show work; critique finding that measures differed between modules.

metrics.name: Datum recorded
metrics.good: datum named for cone data, DEM and aviation inputs
metrics.method: Required field per dataset.
metrics.basis: City DEM description names the CRS (UTM zone 10, NAD83 CSRS) but no vertical datum.

metrics.name: Grid rotation recorded
metrics.good: rotation entered with source (site plan)
metrics.method: Required field; warns when left at default.
metrics.basis: Brief site plan north arrow is rotated against the street grid; value not obtained.

modules.method: 1) Record the assumed block (lat/long) or load the brief's site plan; mark it team assumption. 2) Pick a projected CRS (UTM zone 10, NAD83 CSRS matches the City DEM and open data) with pyproj and store the rotation between the street grid and true north. 3) Sample ground elevation from the City DEM or let the user type it; store the vertical datum of each dataset. 4) For each tower find the reference entrance Z, highest occupied floor, architectural top, tip and highest physical point (plant, window-washing rig, lightning rod). 5) Convert to AGL, AMSL in the chosen datum and CTBUH. 6) Publish site_frame and the height table; downstream modules call convert_height and never convert themselves.
visualization: Table of the height measures per tower with conversion arrows (AGL -> AMSL -> CTBUH)
Vertical ruler diagram: ground, CTBUH reference entrance, highest occupied floor, architectural top, tip, highest physical point
Plan with north arrow showing true north against the street grid; map pin on a City base with the ODP sub-area and cone outlines
outputs: site_frame: {crs, origin, grid_rotation_deg, ground_elev_m, vertical_datum, source_ids, status}
height_table: per tower, all measures, m
highest_point_m: per tower, AGL and AMSL
modules.human_judgment: Choosing the assumed real block and defending it; deciding which entrance is the CTBUH reference; confirming the datum with City staff or the brief package.
modules.limits: The block is hypothetical and the brief's site plan, rotation and station portal are in the gated package. The City DEM (2013 LiDAR, approximate elevations) states no vertical datum; datum offsets are unverified. The AGL ground reference on sloping sites is not defined in the text read.

flags.claim: The View Protection Guidelines are the governing view policy.
flags.correction: Council replaced them with the Public Views Guidelines on 10 Jul 2024: 38 cones cut to 24, view 3.1 removed, 3.2.1-3.2.4 retained. Use post-2024 geometry.
flags.detail: Confirmed by Storeys and by the City open-data set of 24 cones (both opened); the City page is unopened. The scope text and older council documents still use the old name.

flags.claim: P01-M02: 'Sites inside the policy area, buildings up to 600 ft may be considered' is a verified, general threshold.
flags.correction: Policy heights are site-specific (policy Figure 1). 600 ft (183 m) is verified only for the sites immediately across the street from Bay Parkade; elsewhere it is unverified. M02 now stores a lookup, status unverified until the PDF is read.
flags.detail: The City FAQ (opened 21 Oct 2026) says 'sites immediately across the street are within the policy area, where buildings up to 600ft (183 m) may be considered'; Bay Parkade itself lies outside the policy area. The packet's own summaries of the 2011 and 2018 policy (S08, S09, unopened) give about 700 ft on Georgia/Burrard/Granville and 425-500 ft at bridgeheads. Evidence: https://www.shapeyourcity.ca/higher-buildings/widgets/224666/faqs

flags.claim: P01-M05: The YVR zoning surface penetration metric is 'verified' for this tower.
flags.correction: Formula verified; applicability to downtown unknown (probably outside current zoning). The July 2026 proposal adds an area to the 2024 one and its surfaces are unpublished.
flags.detail: SOR/80-902 places the outer limits mainly in Richmond and along the Richmond-Vancouver boundary, and approach surfaces follow runway centrelines. The April 2024 Gazette proposal describes a 4 km outer plane and names Richmond City Centre, Marpole, East Fraser Lands, Big Bend and Delta; downtown is not mentioned. No opened source puts the downtown peninsula inside current zoning. Evidence: https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-80-902/FullText.html ; https://gazette.gc.ca/rp-pr/p1/2024/2024-04-27/html/reg5-eng.html

flags.claim: P01-M04: Pre-2024 cone data overstates restriction for the QEP tests.
flags.correction: Record retained, updated or eliminated per cone. For retained QEP cones 3.2.1-3.2.4 pre-2024 geometry may be unchanged: accept it with an 'unverified, confirm unchanged' badge. Do not test eliminated cones.
flags.detail: Storeys lists QEP views 3.2.1-3.2.4 as retained and none of the QEP views among the 11 updated cones; only 3.1 and 3.2.4a were eliminated. Global News reports a staff recommendation to reduce the bottom of the QEP cone without naming the view or saying it was adopted. City open data now holds 24 polygons including 3.2.1-3.2.4. Evidence: https://storeys.com/vancouver-view-cones-policy-change/ ; https://globalnews.ca/news/10604105/protected-views-vancouver

flags.claim: P01-M05: The precedent screening flag is 288 m above grade.
flags.correction: 288 m is a display marker labelled 'height measure unstated' in the height ladder of P01-M08; it is not a threshold and not on M05's pass/fail cards.
flags.detail: Daily Hive gives 1,034 ft (315 m) with a possible cut of about 88 ft to 946 ft (288 m), attributed to City staff relaying NAV CANADA; it states no datum and names no constraint beyond 'federal aviation requirements'. The issue is specific to the Bay Parkade block. Evidence: https://dailyhive.com/vancouver/holborn-bay-parkade-vancouver-supertall-tower-nav-canada-federal-aviation

flags.claim: P01-M05: NAV CANADA replies take 12-18 months near airports.
flags.correction: Quote the conditional wording; base the metric on whether a request was logged at concept stage; add the Transport Canada Aeronautical Assessment Form (at least 90 days before construction) as a separate checklist item.
flags.detail: NAV CANADA 'attempts to respond within 8 to 12 weeks' and 'these times can go up to 12 to 18 months pending necessary mitigations' for a project in or around an airport. It also says Transport Canada reviews obstacles to be marked and lit and that the portal does not connect to Transport Canada. Evidence: https://www.navcanada.ca/en/aeronautical-information/land-use-program.aspx

flags.claim: P01-M01 and P01-M07: The brief rules (244-305 m band, 9.0 non-residential FSR, site size, transit entrance) are 'verified'.
flags.correction: Downgraded to unverified (the two core metrics are marked false_assumption_corrected). The team registers by 29 Oct 2026, downloads the brief and cites page and clause for each rule.
flags.detail: Their only source, S02, is opened=false because the PDF is email-gated. The competition page (S01, opened 21 Oct 2026) states dates, organisers and prizes but no height, FSR, site, transit or board rules. The packet's convention forbids 'verified' without an opened source. Evidence: https://architecturecompetitions.com/vancouvertallchallenge

flags.claim: P01-M08: Mapping benefits to 'cash CAC' is a verified Vancouver Charter statutory mapping (ss. 565.1, 565.13).
flags.correction: Five separate categories: in-kind condition (s.565(1)(f.1), s.565.17), payment in lieu of density-bonus conditions (s.565.13), DCL (s.523D), ACC (s.523E, in-kind s.523M), and policy-based CAC (negotiated; status 'policy, unverified').
flags.detail: s.565.1 sets base plus higher density for amenities and s.565.13 lets a by-law offer payment in place of conditions at estimated capital cost; neither sets Vancouver's negotiated rezoning CAC, which follows City policy (unopened). ACCs are a separate charge and cannot apply where a DCL may be imposed (s.523I(2)) or duplicate amenity conditions (s.565.1(2.1)). Evidence: https://www.bclaws.gov.bc.ca/civix/document/id/complete/statreg/vanch_28 ; https://www.bclaws.gov.bc.ca/civix/document/id/complete/statreg/vanch_256

flags.claim: P01-M08: Bay Parkade is a usable benchmark for a VTC employment-led tower.
flags.correction: Use Bay Parkade only for height beyond policy, aviation risk and benefit scale. Show a precedent-fit note (program, policy-area status, height measure). Never use it for the program mix or the 9.0 non-residential test.
flags.detail: Bay Parkade is a 100% hotel tower plus residential towers and a social housing tower, with no office (Daily Hive, Storeys), and it lies outside the Higher Buildings policy area (City FAQ). Storey counts conflict: Storeys gives 63 (north), 79 (south), 68 (hotel); Daily Hive gives 68 for the hotel; Construction Canada gives 79 for the hotel. Evidence: https://dailyhive.com/vancouver/holborn-vancouver-western-canada-tallest-tower-bay-parkade-redevelopment-approved ; https://storeys.com/holborn-vancouver-supertall-council-approved/

flags.claim: YVR airport zoning caps downtown tower heights.
flags.detail: Current SOR/80-902 outer limits are described mainly in Richmond and along the Richmond-Vancouver boundary; no source says downtown is inside. Transport Canada's July 2026 proposal adds an area covering much of Vancouver north of the Fraser to the April 2024 proposal; surface heights are unpublished and treatment of existing buildings is not stated for it. Bay Parkade shows that aviation can still cut height, but the constraint was relayed only as 'federal aviation requirements'.

flags.claim: Higher Buildings Policy height range is about 550-700 ft in the CBD.
flags.detail: From search summaries of the 2011 and 2018 versions; the City FAQ (opened) gives 600 ft only for the sites across from Bay Parkade. Read the policy PDF (Shape Your City document link). The adoption date also differs between summaries (22 Apr vs 6 May 1997); amendments cited: 2003, 2011, 2018.

flags.claim: Do hotel, cultural/civic and public-oriented floor area count toward the 9.0 non-residential minimum, and on which ledger (gross or zoning)?
flags.detail: Brief says 'office, commercial'. P01-M01 and P01-M07 now show three tiers side by side (office; plus retail and service incl. hotel; plus cultural/civic, public and non-residential amenity), with residential amenity never counted and core/mechanical shared out by switch. Ask Buildner before the Q&A closes on 3 Nov 2026; registration closes 29 Oct 2026.

flags.claim: Which height measure and which towers must lie inside 244-305 m?
flags.detail: Brief wording is 'one or more towers in the range'. Default is strict: every tower, CTBUH architectural top above the lowest significant pedestrian entrance (P01-M09). Put the question, including the datum, to Buildner by 3 Nov 2026.

flags.claim: Downtown tower separation is 24.4 m (80 ft) and floor plates are capped near 6,500 sq ft.
flags.detail: Recalled from Downtown South practice and residential only; not found or opened. The critic notes it must not be applied to CBD office or hotel towers. Shown only as editable residential candidates in P01-M06; office and hotel bands return unknown until the team enters a band.

flags.claim: Queen Elizabeth cone floors near downtown are about 100-145 m geodetic.
flags.detail: Derived from older documents: 322.8 ft (1997, 1989 cones), 361 ft (2022), 332 ft (2020), and 123-143 m (1070 Barclay); all unopened and pre-2024 or site-specific. The City's open view-cone data (opened) holds polygons only and no elevation fields. Use the Public Views Guidelines or a City View Cone Assessment.

flags.claim: Bay Parkade tower heights and storeys.
flags.detail: City FAQ gives 238.59, 270.97 and 314.89 m. Storeys: north 63, south 79, hotel 68; Daily Hive: hotel 68 storeys, 315 m; Construction Canada: hotel 79 storeys. FSR 27.4 comes from Storeys only. Use as a precedent range only.

flags.claim: Where is the hypothetical block, and what vertical datum do cone elevations use?
flags.detail: Cone, zoning, ODP sub-area and airspace results all depend on an assumed real location and datum (CGVD28 vs CGVD2013 not confirmed; the City DEM states none). P01-M09 records one assumption and its datum; the team must fix it.

flags.claim: Do the City's rezoning policies for large sites, the CAC policy and the Metro Core jobs policy apply to a block of about 1.15 ha?
flags.detail: Not opened: City hosts blocked and search quota ran out. The critic recalls a large-sites policy at 0.8 ha or 45,000 m2 (unverified). Also unknown whether VTC's 9.0 non-residential minimum mirrors an ODP or Metro Core rule.

flags.claim: CBD land use: residential is restricted in the CBD core and job space is protected (Metro Core Jobs and Economy Land Use Plan).
flags.detail: Reviewer recollection; no source opened (City hosts 403; the Vancouver Plan and ODP pages do not mention it). If true, the brief's residential share is a policy departure. Plan date unconfirmed (reviewer recalls 2009). New city-wide Vancouver ODP (31 Mar 2026) replaced the Vancouver Plan; its effect on this policy is unread.

flags.claim: Rezoning Policy for Sustainable Large Developments applies at 0.8 ha or 45,000 m2.
flags.detail: Reviewer recollection, not opened. VTC block is about 1.15 ha with over 103,000 m2 non-residential area, so both thresholds would be met if recalled correctly. Required measures (sustainable site design, green mobility, rainwater, zero waste, low-carbon energy, affordable housing) are also recalled only.

flags.claim: Green Buildings Policy for Rezonings, the public art requirement for rezonings and the Bird Friendly Design Guidelines apply to this scheme.
flags.detail: Reviewer recollection; none opened and no numbers given. Registered as pointer rows: energy and emissions to ENER, bird-friendly design to ECOL, public art as a benefit category in P01-M08.

flags.claim: The Zoning and Development By-law lists Hotel under Service Uses (so hotel is commercial for the 9.0 test).
flags.detail: Reviewer recollection; the by-law returned HTTP 403. Ordinary usage also treats hotel as commercial. P01-M07 keeps hotel in tier 2 and shows tier 1 (office only) beside it.

flags.claim: The VTC block lies in a transit-oriented area, so residential parking minimums are zero.
flags.detail: The Province's page (opened) sets TOAs within 800 m of a rapid transit station and bars residential parking requirements there; Vancouver's TOA designation by-law and map were not read. The brief places a station beside the site; City open data holds Burrard, Granville, Vancouver City Centre and Waterfront stations. Commercial parking and loading may still be required.

flags.claim: Central CBD blocks fall inside Queen Elizabeth Park cone polygons.
flags.detail: Team-derived on 21 Oct 2026 from City open data: sampled intersections (Georgia/Burrard, Georgia/Granville, Hastings/Burrard, Pender/Howe, Nelson/Burrard) fell inside polygons 3.2.1, 3.2.2 or 3.2.3. Coordinates were approximate and the polygons are 2D, so this shows the cone floor is the likely binding cap, not a result for any block. Re-run on the assumed block.

flags.claim: Does the brief package (site plan, 3D model) include a real location, view cones or the station portal point?
flags.detail: Not checked: the package is email-gated. If it does, P01-M04 and P01-M09 use it as the default dataset (source S02); if not, hypothetical-cone mode gives the QEP render without pass/fail.

flags.claim: Heliport, harbour water aerodrome and instrument-procedure constraints on downtown towers.
flags.detail: No heliport was identified (HeliJet heliport near the harbour flight centre; hospital pads possible); CYHC lane layout and NAV CANADA instrument-procedure obstacle clearance were not found. Carried as named unknowns in P01-M05; Standard 325 is a certification standard, so penetration is an operator-impact flag, not a ban.

flags.claim: Standard 621 details (90 days notice, CL-856 spacing, daytime marking above 150 m AGL).
flags.detail: Read through a summarising fetch of the first 200,000 of 233,211 characters; CAR s.601.23-601.24 were read directly. Confirm exact clause wording in the text before citing on a board.

flags.claim: Does the Vancouver ODP (31 Mar 2026) change downtown height, job-space or tower-design policy?
flags.detail: The Shape Your City ODP page says the plan builds on and replaces the Vancouver Plan and gives no downtown detail; the PDF is blocked. Register row added, content unread.
